title: Desk Rule — One Live Automation Plan per Building under the Building Automation Service Plans
content:
# Desk Rule — One Live Automation Plan per Building under the Building Automation Service Plans

**The rule the desk applies.** A building owner may hold several Building Automation Service Plans, one for each building whose controls system the company supports, and the portfolio is counted whenever a plan is priced or a shared entitlement is drawn. A second plan is not quoted for a site that already holds a plan in quoted, active, pending renewal or suspended status; the covered points of that site are amended instead. Plans in expired, cancelled or declined status do not block a fresh quote. Support hours, alarm responses and balances are held per plan and are never pooled across sites, even where one owner holds plans at every building in a campus, because each plan covers one controls database.

**Points of judgement.**

1. There is no ceiling on the number of plans one owner may hold: the count is one plan per supported building, not a number per customer.
2. Whether a site already holds a plan is read from the plan records, before a quote is opened, by matching the building: a plan record for that same building in quoted, active, pending renewal or suspended status blocks a second quote for it. What the caller says about the building's cover does not stand in for the record.
3. The blocked case is answered by amending the covered points of the plan that already exists, not by opening a new one.

**Status table for a building that already holds a plan.**

| Status of the existing plan at that building | Fresh quote for the same building |
|---|---|
| quoted | not opened; covered points amended instead |
| active | not opened; covered points amended instead |
| pending renewal | not opened; covered points amended instead |
| suspended | not opened; covered points amended instead |
| expired | may be quoted |
| cancelled | may be quoted |
| declined | may be quoted |

**Per-plan entitlements.** Two buildings of one owner each hold their own support hour pool, their own alarm response allowance and their own balance. As a hypothetical, an owner with an exhausted pool at one building and unused hours at another cannot have the second building's hours drawn for the first: each plan covers one controls database.
